It is the largest managed health care company in the Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) Association serving more than 112 million individuals across 14 states. A regular in Fortune 500 list, Elevance Health ranked 18 in 2026. Gail Boudreaux , President and CEO of Elevance Health has been a consistent name in the Fortune list of most powerful women and currently holds 81st rank on this list. ABOUT CARELON GLOBAL SOLUTIONS Carelon Global Solutions (CGS) is a healthcare solutions company simplifying complex operational processes to improve the health of the healthcare system. Previously known as Legato Health Technologies, Carelon Global Solutions (hereinafter, CGS) underwent a name change and joined the Carelon family of brands in January 2023, as a fully owned subsidiary of Elevance Health (Previously Anthem Inc.). CGS brings together a global team of like-minded innovators who manage and optimize operational processes for health plans as well as providers. Our brightest minds housed across our global headquarters in Indianapolis as well as Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Gurugram in India, Manila in the Philippines, and San Juan in Puerto Rico bring with them innovative capabilities and an unmatched depth of experience. This global team uniquely positions CGS to enable scalable, next-generation platforms and specialized digital tools that make healthcare operations more practical, effective, and efficient. OUR MISSION & VALUES Our Mission: Improving Lives and Communities. Simplifying Healthcare. Expecting More.
 Our Values: Leadership | Community | Integrity | Agility | Diversity JOB PURPOSE Carelon Global Solutions India is seeking a Senior Manager Architecture to lead architecture and end-to-end implementation of enterprise pharmacy management capabilities for CarelonRx. The role owns technical vision, solution architecture, engineering execution, implementation readiness, and platform outcomes across complex, multi-system pharmacy transformation programs. The position is intentionally weighted toward architecture, engineering, AI-enabled Spec-Driven Development, and large-scale implementation leadership. Delivery administration is a supporting responsibility, not the primary mandate. The leader will combine strong software engineering depth with practical pharmacy and PBM domain knowledge to translate business capabilities into secure, scalable, resilient, and operable platforms. JOB RESPONSIBILITY Enterprise Pharmacy Architecture Define and govern target-state solution architecture for end-to-end pharmacy management systems, aligned with enterprise architecture, security, data, privacy, resiliency, and regulatory guardrails. Create capability maps, domain boundaries, reference architectures, reusable patterns, integration standards, and modernization roadmaps across the pharmacy ecosystem. Lead architecture decisions for microservices, APIs, event streaming, workflow orchestration, data platforms, cloud-native services, observability, and interoperability with legacy platforms. Own architecture reviews, trade-off decisions, non-functional requirements, technical debt strategy, and design assurance from concept through production adoption. End-To-End Pharmacy Platform Implementation Lead implementation across relevant pharmacy and PBM capabilities such as benefit configuration, formulary, eligibility, claims adjudication, pricing, prior authorization, pharmacy networks, specialty pharmacy, clinical programs, rebates, member and provider experiences, and operational reporting. Translate business journeys and pharmacy operating models into domain-aligned services, data contracts, interfaces, implementation increments, migration plans, and measurable acceptance criteria. Own the technical implementation lifecycle covering discovery, architecture, engineering, integration, data conversion, testing strategy, cutover, production readiness, stabilization, and benefits realization. Manage cross-platform dependencies and ensure that application, data, infrastructure, security, operations, and vendor workstreams converge into one implementable solution. Drive phased rollout, coexistence, migration, and decommissioning strategies that protect member, client, pharmacy, and operational continuity. AI-Enabled Spec-Driven Development (SDD) Establish an AI-first Spec-Driven Development approach in which approved business, architecture, interface, security, testing, and operational specifications become the governed source for implementation. Enable engineering agents and copilots to accelerate design elaboration, code generation, test creation, documentation, code review, traceability, and impact analysis, with human review and approval at critical control points. Define reusable SDD templates, prompt and context standards, repository conventions, quality gates, evaluation criteria, and responsible AI controls for enterprise adoption. Measure SDD outcomes using baselines and agreed targets for engineering cycle time, specification-to-code traceability, automated test coverage, escaped defects, rework, deployment frequency, and productivity improvement. Ensure AI-generated artifacts meet enterprise standards for security, privacy, intellectual property, explainability, maintainability, and auditability. Engineering Excellence And Hands-On Technical Leadership Provide credible, hands-on technical leadership through design reviews, code and API reviews, proof-of-concept direction, critical problem solving, performance analysis, and production diagnostics. Guide teams on software design principles, domain-driven design, secure coding, automated testing, DevSecOps, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, reliability engineering, and cloud cost optimization. Define engineering scorecards and quality gates covering code health, architecture compliance, security vulnerabilities, reliability, performance, recoverability, maintainability, and operational readiness. Champion platform engineering, reusable services, developer experience, automated environments, and self-service capabilities that reduce implementation friction at scale. Large-Scale Implementation Leadership Lead multiple engineering teams and technical workstreams across product, architecture, software engineering, data, quality engineering, cloud, security, operations, and partner organizations. Create an integrated technical implementation plan that connects architecture runway, dependency sequencing, environment readiness, test strategy, migration, cutover, and operational acceptance. Act as the senior technical decision-maker for complex implementation risks, cross-team conflicts, architecture exceptions, integration failures, and production-readiness gaps. Provide transparent executive-level reporting on architecture health, implementation progress, critical dependencies, risk exposure, quality, readiness, and realized business outcomes. Build governance that is lightweight but effective, emphasizing decision velocity, measurable technical outcomes, and removal of systemic blockers rather than delivery administration. Pharmacy Domain And Stakeholder Partnership Apply working knowledge of the prescription lifecycle, PBM operations, payer and pharmacy interactions, clinical and utilization management, drug data, pricing, formulary, claims, and applicable industry transactions and regulations. Partner with pharmacy business leaders, product managers, enterprise architects, security, operations, compliance, and client teams to shape solutions that are technically sound and operationally adoptable. Convert domain policies, rules, and exceptions into explicit specifications, testable requirements, decision services, and traceable implementation controls. Challenge assumptions using outside-in engineering and pharmacy-platform practices while tailoring recommendations to CarelonRx business priorities and enterprise constraints. People And Capability Leadership Build, lead, and mentor engineering managers, solution architects, principal engineers, technical leads, developers, quality engineers, and platform specialists across distributed teams. Establish clear technical accountabilities, architecture ownership, engineering career paths, succession plans, and communities of practice for pharmacy engineering and AI SDD. Create a culture of engineering rigor, transparent decision-making, experimentation, learning, inclusion, and accountability for outcomes. Assess capability gaps and execute hiring, upskilling, partner augmentation, and workforce plans required for large-scale implementation. Delivery Governance As A Supporting Responsibility Partner with product and program leadership on planning, investment sequencing, release readiness, dependency management, and risk escalation. Use delivery metrics only as supporting indicators. Primary accountability remains architecture quality, end-to-end implementation integrity, engineering excellence, and business capability outcomes. Ensure commitments are realistic, technically grounded, and supported by clear specifications, measurable acceptance criteria, and production-readiness evidence. QUALIFICATION Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline; postgraduate qualification is preferred. Strong foundation in software engineering, enterprise solution architecture, systems integration, cloud engineering, data architecture, cybersecurity, and operational resilience. Demonstrated ability to communicate architecture and implementation choices to business executives, product leaders, engineers, risk partners, and external vendors. Ability to lead through ambiguity, make evidence-based trade-offs, and connect pharmacy business outcomes to technical architecture and implementation decisions. Working knowledge of Agile, product operating models, DevSecOps, secure SDLC, and modern engineering governance. EXPERIENCE 15+ years of progressive experience in software engineering, solution architecture, enterprise platforms, and technology implementation, including 5+ years leading engineering managers, architects, or large technical teams. Proven leadership of large-scale, multi-year enterprise implementations involving multiple applications, complex integrations, data migration, cloud platforms, distributed teams, and production cutover. Relevant healthcare, pharmacy, or PBM experience, with demonstrable understanding of end-to-end pharmacy capabilities and their technology implications. Demonstrated experience defining target architecture and taking complex platforms from architecture through implementation, production readiness, stabilization, and measurable adoption. Experience applying AI-assisted engineering, Spec-Driven Development, agentic workflows, or comparable automation across the SDLC with appropriate human oversight and governance. Experience managing strategic vendors and globally distributed teams while retaining internal ownership of architecture, engineering quality, and implementation outcomes. Experience modernizing legacy systems using APIs, microservices, event-driven patterns, cloud-native platforms, automated testing, DevSecOps, observability, and reliability practices. SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES Core Technical Competencies Enterprise and solution architecture; domain-driven design; capability modeling; microservices; API-first and event-driven architecture; integration and interoperability patterns. Java and/or .NET engineering ecosystems; REST and GraphQL APIs; event-streaming platforms; containers and Kubernetes; Azure and/or AWS; CI/CD; infrastructure as code; observability and SRE practices. Data architecture, master and reference data, transactional and analytical data patterns, data quality, lineage, privacy, and secure information exchange. Previously known as Legato Health Technologies, Carelon Global Solutions (hereinafter, CGS) underwent a name change and joined the Carelon family of brands in January 2023, as a fully owned subsidiary of Elevance Health (Previously Anthem Inc.). CGS brings together a global team of like-minded innovators who manage and optimize operational processes for health plans as well as providers. Our brightest minds housed across our global headquarters in Indianapolis as well as Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Gurugram in India, Manila in the Philippines, and San Juan in Puerto Rico bring with them innovative capabilities and an unmatched depth of experience. This global team uniquely positions CGS to enable scalable, next-generation platforms and specialized digital tools that make healthcare operations more practical, effective, and efficient. OUR MISSION & VALUES Our Mission: Improving Lives and Communities. Simplifying Healthcare. Expecting More.
 Our Values: Leadership | Community | Integrity | Agility | Diversity JOB PURPOSE Carelon Global Solutions India is seeking a Senior Manager Architecture to lead architecture and end-to-end implementation of enterprise pharmacy management capabilities for CarelonRx. The role owns technical vision, solution architecture, engineering execution, implementation readiness, and platform outcomes across complex, multi-system pharmacy transformation programs. The position is intentionally weighted toward architecture, engineering, AI-enabled Spec-Driven Development, and large-scale implementation leadership. Delivery administration is a supporting responsibility, not the primary mandate. The leader will combine strong software engineering depth with practical pharmacy and PBM domain knowledge to translate business capabilities into secure, scalable, resilient, and operable platforms. JOB RESPONSIBILITY Enterprise Pharmacy Architecture Define and govern target-state solution architecture for end-to-end pharmacy management systems, aligned with enterprise architecture, security, data, privacy, resiliency, and regulatory guardrails. Create capability maps, domain boundaries, reference architectures, reusable patterns, integration standards, and modernization roadmaps across the pharmacy ecosystem. Lead architecture decisions for microservices, APIs, event streaming, workflow orchestration, data platforms, cloud-native services, observability, and interoperability with legacy platforms. Own architecture reviews, trade-off decisions, non-functional requirements, technical debt strategy, and design assurance from concept through production adoption. End-To-End Pharmacy Platform Implementation Lead implementation across relevant pharmacy and PBM capabilities such as benefit configuration, formulary, eligibility, claims adjudication, pricing, prior authorization, pharmacy networks, specialty pharmacy, clinical programs, rebates, member and provider experiences, and operational reporting. Translate business journeys and pharmacy operating models into domain-aligned services, data contracts, interfaces, implementation increments, migration plans, and measurable acceptance criteria. Own the technical implementation lifecycle covering discovery, architecture, engineering, integration, data conversion, testing strategy, cutover, production readiness, stabilization, and benefits realization. Manage cross-platform dependencies and ensure that application, data, infrastructure, security, operations, and vendor workstreams converge into one implementable solution. Drive phased rollout, coexistence, migration, and decommissioning strategies that protect member, client, pharmacy, and operational continuity. AI-Enabled Spec-Driven Development (SDD) Establish an AI-first Spec-Driven Development approach in which approved business, architecture, interface, security, testing, and operational specifications become the governed source for implementation. title: Engineer 3 - Business Systems
description:
The CRM Technologies team builds, scales, and operates Salesforce-based solutions that power MongoDBs customer lifecycle, from marketing engagement and lead management through sales execution, account management, renewals, reporting, and downstream operational workflows. 
 The team partners closely with Marketing, Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Finance, Customer Success, Data, and Engineering to deliver secure, scalable, and reliable business systems. The team continuously evolves the CRM and marketing technology ecosystem through automation, integrations, data quality improvements, and platform operations. 
 Role Overview 
 We are looking for an Engineer III, Business Systems to design, build, and support the systems and integrations that enable MongoDBs top-of-funnel and lead-to-revenue processes. 
 This individual contributor role will focus on marketing technology, lead lifecycle management, enrichment, campaign operations, account and territory management, activity management, outreach, annual planning, and inbound and outbound integrations. You will translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions using Salesforce, marketing automation platforms, integration tools, APIs, and data services. 
 You will own delivery across the full solution lifecycle, including requirements analysis, solution design, development, testing, deployment, documentation, monitoring, and production support. You will also contribute to engineering standards, platform governance, data quality, and continuous improvement across the GTM Technology ecosystem. 
 We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Gurugram for our hybrid working model. 
 What Youll Do 
 
 Design, build, and support solutions for top-of-funnel and marketing operations processes 
 Develop and enhance lead capture, lead conversion, routing, qualification, scoring, and lifecycle management capabilities 
 Administer and integrate marketing and enrichment platforms such as FCI, LeanData, Ortoo, and related GTM applications 
 Build and maintain integrations between Salesforce, marketing automation, enrichment, outreach, analytics, data, and downstream business systems 
 Support campaign management, campaign attribution, audience segmentation, campaign member management, and marketing performance workflows 
 Develop scalable solutions for account management, territory planning, account assignment, ownership changes, and coverage models 
 Design and support partner management capabilities, including partner onboarding, partner data management, partner lifecycle workflows, referral and lead registration processes, partner attribution, and partner communications 
 Build and enhance partner portal experiences that provide secure access to leads, opportunities, campaign resources, enablement content, deal registration, performance insights, and relevant account information 
 Enable activity management and Outreach workflows across marketing, business development, sales, and partner teams 
 Design and support inbound integrations that create, enrich, qualify, and route leads and accounts into Salesforce 
 Partner with Marketing Operations, Sales Development, Sales Operations, RevenueOperations, Data, and Engineering to understand requirements and identify process gaps 
 Contribute to documentation, UAT, regression testing, runbooks, monitoring, and user enablement 
 Leverage AI-powered engineering tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, Agentforce, and GitHub Copilot to improve productivity, analysis, troubleshooting, and documentation while applying sound judgment around security, privacy, and accuracy 
 
 Responsibilities 
 Technical Delivery 
 
 Translate business requirements into scalable marketing technology and Salesforce solutions using declarative configuration, custom development, APIs, and integration platforms. 
 
 Marketing Technology Engineering 
 
 Own and enhance capabilities across:
 
 Lead capture, conversion, qualification, and routing 
 Marketing enrichment and data normalization 
 Campaign and campaign member management 
 Account identification, matching, and hierarchy management 
 Territory planning and account assignment 
 Activity and engagement management 
 Outreach and business development workflows 
 Marketing attribution and lifecycle reporting 
 Annual planning and operational planning processes 
 
 
 
 Integration and System Design 
 
 Design and support secure, reliable, and observable inbound and outbound integrations across Salesforce, marketing automation, enrichment, outreach, analytics, and enterprise platforms. 
 
 Data Quality and Governance 
 
 Establish reliable data flows and controls that improve completeness, accuracy, consistency, deduplication, consent handling, and governance across lead, contact, account, campaign, and activity data. 
 
 Engineering Excellence 
 
 Maintain high standards for modular design, test coverage, documentation, deployment processes, monitoring, CI/CD, and adherence to shared integration and Salesforce engineering patterns. 
 
 Platform Optimization 
 
 Proactively identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, integration risks, manual processes, technical debt, and opportunities to simplify the marketing technology architecture. 
 
 Minimum Requirements 
 
 Bachelors or Masters degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience 
 6+ years of hands-on Salesforce development or enterprise business systems engineering experience 
 Strong experience with Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flows, SOQL, Salesforce APIs, and platform automation 
 Proficiency in scripting and programming languages such as Python and JavaScript, with experience building reusable automation, data transformation, and integration services 
 Experience with React or comparable modern front-end frameworks 
 Experience with full-stack development, including front-end applications, back-end services, APIs, data models, authentication, testing, deployment, and operational support 
 Experience designing and supporting marketing technology, CRM, lead management, or revenue operations solutions 
 Experience building and supporting REST or SOAP API integrations and data synchronization processes 
 Strong understanding of Salesforce security, data governance, data quality, and scalable implementation practices 
 Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, and collaboration skills 
 Salesforce Platform Developer I or II certification required 
 
 Success Measures 
 In 3 Months 
 Develop a strong understanding of MongoDBs marketing technology and Salesforce architecture, top-of-funnel processes, lead lifecycle, campaign operations, integration landscape, and stakeholder environment. 
 In 6 Months 
 Deliver meaningful enhancements across lead management, marketing integrations, enrichment, campaign management, routing, account management, or related GTM Technology initiatives. Establish yourself as a dependable technical contributor and trusted partner to Marketing Operations and Revenue Operations. 
 In 12 Months 
 Become a trusted subject matter expert for marketing technology and top-of-funnel business systems. Drive scalable improvements across lead conversion, enrichment, campaign operations, territory planning, outreach, data quality, and inbound and outbound integrations while influencing engineering standards and platform strategy. 
 About MongoDB 
 MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDBs unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. 
 With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including AI-native startups and approximately 75% of the Fortune 100, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, were powering the next era of software.

From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy, we value our employeeswellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys.  The Design Manager is responsible for leading the design engineering function, 
 overseeing end-to-end design operations from initial concept through production 
 handoff. This role blends technical leadership, design validation, resource planning, 
 and cross-functional coordination with manufacturing, quality, and project 
 management teams to ensure deliverables meet functional, aesthetic, quality, and 
 budgetary requirements.

 Design Leadership & Project Execution: Lead, mentor, and allocate work across the

 standardized design libraries, revision control, and Product Data Management 
 (PDM/PLM) protocols. 
 Design Validation & Compliance: 
 Conduct thorough Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) 
 reviews prior to tooling and fabrication release. Ensure engineering calculations, 
 tolerance stack-up analyses, and simulations (FEA/stress analysis) comply with 
 functional and safety standards. Verify that all technical documentation, engineering 
 change orders (ECOs), and production drawings adhere to applicable industry 
 standards (ISO, ASME, DIN). 
 Cross-Functional & Vendor Coordination: 
 Collaborate closely with production, tooling, and fabrication units to resolve design- 
 related issues on the shop floor. Coordinate with vendors, prototype developers, and 
 component suppliers regarding material specifications, tooling feasibility, and sample 
 approvals. Support the quality control team by establishing inspection benchmarks, 
 critical-to-quality (CTQ) dimensions, and testing parameters. 
 Process Improvement & Team Development: 
 Implement best practices in CAD automation, modeling standards, and digital workflow 
 optimization. Drive continuous cost-reduction initiatives through value engineering 
 and material optimization. Conduct periodic technical training and performance 
 reviews for junior engineers and draftsmen. 
 Performance Indicators (KPIs ) 
 On-Time Release: Punctual delivery of design freezes, production drawings, and ECO 
 approvals. 
 First-Time-Right (FTR) Rate: Minimization of design revisions post-tooling or during 
 pilot production. 
 Cost & Weight Optimization: Measurable reductions in material usage or manufacturing 
 cycle time via value engineering. 
 Team Throughput: Effective task distribution and development of team capabilities.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Infrastructure,Kubernetes
description:
Job Description About the role We are hiring a staff software engineer (IC4) for the Telemetry Data Platform team, which carries product usage telemetry for the entire ServiceNow platform on a stack built with Kubernetes, Kafka, and ClickHouse. We are distributed across Israel, India, and the Americas. This is a full stack role with its center of gravity firmly on the infrastructure side - expect roughly two-thirds of your time on telemetry infrastructure, data pipelines, Kubernetes and DevOps work, and the rest on the services and product surfaces on top. You will be equally comfortable designing a distributed system and owning it in production. If you like following a system from the event that fires to the chart that renders - and you want the pager for it - you will feel at home. You will lead design and delivery of complex, multi-service features, own technical decisions within a domain, and are fully self-directed - escalating only genuine ambiguities and driving decisions to closure. Of the ten critical skills at this level, incident response management is the only one set at Expert; the rest are Experienced. What you ll do Telemetry infrastructure and data pipelines Design, build, and own backend services for distributed data streaming and processing that handle high-volume, high-cardinality event data with predictable latency and no silent data loss. Build and maintain Kafka-based streaming pipelines and the pipeline components that feed ClickHouse. Own data modeling and query performance in ClickHouse - partitioning, sort keys, materialized views, retention, and the cost curve that comes with all of it. Partner with product and platform teams to shape requirements for telemetry ingestion and processing, then drive the solutions to production. Kubernetes, DevOps, and production ownership Deploy, scale, and operate services in production Kubernetes environments, including Helm-based deployments and CI/CD pipelines that make releases repeatable and safe to roll back. Own observability for what you build - meaningful metrics, useful logs, real tracing, and alerts that fire on customer impact rather than on noise. Debug and resolve production incidents independently, participate in on-call, run root-cause analysis, and operate against defined service level objectives. Full stack engineering and technical leadership Own the full development lifecycle for your work, and build the backend services and APIs that expose telemetry to internal consumers, product surfaces, and AI agents - including API contracts, data models, and schema migrations. Contribute to the analytics front end - dashboards, funnels, and exploration tools - with an eye on performance against large result sets, and improve the web and mobile capture SDKs. title: Senior Atlassian Admin
description:
About Rightsline: 
 At Rightsline, we are redefining how the global media and entertainment industry manages and monetizes intellectual property. Since 2012, Rightsline has been trusted by some of the worlds most influential studios, broadcasters, and content owners to simplify the complex world of rights and royalties through powerful, intelligent technology. 
 Our cloud-based, fully integrated platform provides a single source of truth for managing rights, royalties, contracts, and financial workflows across markets, territories, and distribution channels. By bringing together data, automation, and collaboration in one configurable ecosystem, we enable organizations to unlock the full value of their content portfolios while operating with greater transparency, efficiency, and control. 
 At Rightsline, we combine deep industry expertise with cutting-edge technology to solve complex challenges at scale. Our teams work at the intersection of technology, media, and innovation—building solutions that power the business of content worldwide. 
 Joining Rightsline means becoming part of a collaborative, forward-thinking environment where your ideas, expertise, and contributions directly shape the future of rights and royalties management. If you are passionate about building impactful technology and working alongside talented global teams, Rightsline offers the platform to grow, innovate, and make a meaningful difference. 
 What You Will Own: 
 Instance Configuration & Governance Own all shared configuration in our company-managed Jira Cloud instance: custom fields, screens and screen schemes, field configurations, workflows and workflow schemes, work types and hierarchy levels, priorities, resolutions, and permission and notification schemes. Apply and enforce the discipline company-managed Jira requires establish whether an object is shared before changing it, and when it is, copy it, scope the copy to the project, and change the copy. Most instance damage comes from skipping this step. Own and maintain all the Atlassian sister products like Confluence, Jira Service Desk, and Jira Product Discovery Maintain naming conventions that make configuration ownership obvious at a glance, and run a recurring audit that catches projects drifting back onto shared objects. Keep the custom-field estate from growing unchecked: reuse before creating, scope through field contexts rather than editing shared ones, and retire fields no longer in use. Own project creation and decommissioning, and grant permissions to project roles rather than named individuals so access survives staffing changes. 
 Workflow, Automation & App Administration Translate how teams actually work into workflow, status, and board configuration and propose the lighter alternative when a request is better solved by a convention than by new configuration. Publish workflow changes safely, including migrating in-flight work when statuses change, and keep board column mappings in step so nothing lands in an unmapped state. Build and maintain Jira Automation rules, scoped correctly so one team's rule does not surface in another team's menus. Administer our Marketplace apps including their own scoping settings, and evaluate new apps before they become permanent. 
 Confluence & Process Documentation Own Confluence spaces, permissions, templates, and page hierarchy. Partner with engineering leads to get our delivery process written down and kept current: status definitions with owners and exit criteria, work-type guidance, Definition of Ready and Definition of Done, and branch-naming requirements. Company-managed Jira cannot hold per-project helper text, so Confluence is where this lives. Write short, durable runbooks for recurring requests, and train team leads to self-serve the routine changes. 
 Reporting, Data & Integrations Protect the conventions our delivery metrics depend on — the estimation field, status names, issue-key format, and what counts as a defect. Breaking one of these produces wrong numbers rather than an error message, so you are the last line of defence. Own the data contract behind our delivery-analytics platform (Plandek): which fields and statuses it reads, and what a rename would cost. Write JQL that answers non-trivial questions, build filters and dashboards, and run bulk changes safely. Use the Jira Cloud REST API for work with no UI path — bulk version creation, field inventories, and pulling issue changelogs for time-in-status and flow metrics. Changelog data cannot be reached through CSV export, so this is a working requirement rather than a bonus. Maintain the Jira–Git integration that drives status transitions, along with the Zendesk, Salesforce, and Sentry connectors. 
 Access, Compliance & Support Produce access-review and change-management evidence for SOC 2: who holds admin rights, who holds elevated issue permissions, and what changed when. Own Atlassian onboarding and offboarding, licence allocation, and seat cost management. Be the first and last stop for “Jira is broken” — diagnosing with the tooling (permission helper, automation audit logs) rather than reasoning from first principles, since most reports resolve to a handful of known causes. Collaborating with cross-functional teams Ensure compliance with ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2 frameworks 
 What You Bring: 5+ years administering Atlassian Cloud, including hands-on ownership of a company-managed (not only team-managed) Jira instance where multiple projects share configuration. This is our most important requirement: team-managed-only experience does not transfer, because the whole difficulty of this role is shared configuration. Atlassian Certified Professional (Jira Administration or Jira Service Management). ScriptRunner (Groovy), or comparable depth administering Marketplace apps. Jira Service Management, Atlassian Guard / Access, or Atlassian Analytics. Experience with a delivery-metrics platform (Plandek, LinearB, Jellyfish, Sleuth) and the Jira data hygiene it requires. Having led a team-managed to company-managed migration, or a Server / Data Center to Cloud migration. Familiarity with SOC 2 or comparable audit evidence collection. Exposure to AI-assisted development tooling and how its activity should be represented in Jira. Demonstrated ownership of workflows, screen and field configuration schemes, issue type schemes, and permission schemes — you have built them, published them, and migrated existing issues through a status change. Jira Automation at a competent level: multi-step rules, smart values, branching, and correct rule scoping. Confluence administration: spaces, permissions, and templates. Strong JQL, plus filters, dashboards, and safe bulk operations. Scripting against the Jira REST API in Python, JavaScript, or equivalent, including token authentication, pagination, and changelog extraction. Judgment about blast radius — before changing anything you check what else depends on it, and you can be trusted with an instance twenty teams rely on. Willingness to push back: declining the request that would add a field nobody fills in or a status nobody exits, and proposing the lighter alternative. Clear written communication, a habit of documenting as you go, and experience working effectively with colleagues across time zones. 
 Work Environment & Expectations: Noida/NCR based Demonstrates flexibility to work in required shifts. Regular overlap with US-based engineering leadership, targeting 4 hours daily. Compliance with security and remote working policies

title: Power Platform Technical Lead (Dynamics 365 CE / Dataverse)
description:
Role: Power Platform Technical Lead Location: Remote Shift Hours: 1400 to 2300 hours IST  Job Type: Full-time Experience: 8+ years 


 Role Purpose The Power Platform Technical Lead is the senior technical authority for Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement (CE), Dataverse and the wider Power Platform. The role combines hands-on engineering with technical leadership, defining standards, reviewing code, owning the ALM model and ensuring that everything we build on the platform is scalable, secure and production-ready. The Lead works closely with the Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Solution Architects and the IT Applications Developer team. 
 Key Responsibilities Technical Leadership in D365 & Power Platform Act as technical authority for Dynamics 365 CE and Power Platform solutions, owning architecture decisions, design patterns and non-functional requirements. Mentor IT Applications Developers and citizen makers; raise the technical bar through coaching, design reviews and pairing. Translate business requirements into well-architected Dataverse data models, app designs and integration patterns. Solution Management with Native Git Own the Dataverse Git integration strategy: branch model, solution segmentation, folder structure, commit hygiene and developer onboarding. Maintain repository standards in Azure DevOps Repos (branch policies, PR templates, required reviewers, build validation). Enforce solution layering, managed-properties discipline and unmanaged-customisation block policies. 
 Solution Deployment & Versioning Design and operate deployments through native Power Platform Pipelines (in PPAC) and complementary Azure DevOps (ADO) pipelines for code-first artefacts. Define environment strategy (Dev / Build / Test / UAT / Pre-Prod / Prod) and the promotion path for each solution stream. Govern release versioning, release notes (incl. Copilot-assisted generation), approval gates and hotfix workflows. 
 Flow & Agent Management Provide design and run-time governance for Cloud Flows, Desktop Flows and Copilot/agent flows: connection references, environment variables, error handling, performance, throttling. Define standards for service-principal-owned flows, sharing models and DLP-compliant connector usage. 
 Infrastructure as Code Terraform Maintain Terraform modules for the Azure resources that support Power Platform (resource groups, service principals, Key Vaults, Logic Apps, Function Apps, Storage, App Insights). Review and approve Terraform pull requests; enforce state-management and module-versioning standards. Dynamics CRM Plugins & Extensibility Design, review and maintain Dataverse plugins, custom APIs, custom workflow activities and PCF components in C#/.NET. Set standards for plugin performance (transactions, depth, ILogger, tracing service) and review for security risk. 
 Code Review Standards Be the named code reviewer for high-impact Power Platform, Dataverse and Azure-adjacent changes. Author and continuously improve coding standards covering C#, TypeScript/JavaScript, Power Fx, Dataverse plugins and Logic Apps. Champion the use of solution checker, Power Platform CLI, ESLint/Prettier and SonarCloud. D365 Security Management & Configuration Design Dataverse security roles, business units, teams, field-level security and hierarchy security. Govern security-role version control through solutions and ensure audit-grade traceability of permission changes. Azure Foundations Resource Groups: define naming, tagging and access conventions; review RG-level RBAC. Service Principals: govern lifecycle (creation, secret/cert rotation, expiry monitoring) and least-privilege assignments. Key Vault: manage secret storage standards, access policies / RBAC, integration with Logic Apps, Functions, ADO and Power Platform connection references. 
 Pipeline Deployment for Logic Apps Azure Functions Own the CI/CD pipelines for Logic Apps (Standard and Consumption) and Azure Functions used as Dataverse extensions or integration glue. Define artefact, slot-swap and parameterisation strategy across environments. Integration Tooling Use Postman and SoapUI to design, document and regression-test REST/SOAP integrations to/from Dataverse, 
 F&O and third-party systems. Maintain shared collections and environments for the developer team. Programming Languages C# (.NET 8+) plugins, custom APIs, Azure Functions. TypeScript / JavaScript client-side scripts, PCF components, Logic Apps inline code. Power Fx formula standards across canvas apps and Power Automate. 
 Use of AI Use GitHub Copilot, Copilot in Power Apps / Power Automate / Power Pages and Copilot Studio to accelerate delivery and standardise patterns. Govern responsible AI use data handling, prompt patterns, model selection and review of AI-generated code before merge. Identify opportunities to deploy Copilot Studio agents for internal user support and internal IT operations. 
 Essential Skills & Experience 6+ years in the Microsoft Dynamics CRM / Dataverse ecosystem, with at least 2 years in a lead or senior engineering role. Deep, hands-on experience with Dataverse data modelling, security and extensibility. Production experience with native Power Platform Pipelines and Dataverse Git integration. Strong C# / .NET, TypeScript and Power Fx; comfortable in both pro-code and low-code stacks. Demonstrable Azure experience: Resource Groups, RBAC, Service Principals, Key Vault, Logic Apps, Azure Functions, App Insights. 
 Hands-on Terraform for the supporting Azure footprint. Experience leading code reviews and authoring engineering standards. Proficient with Postman and SoapUI for integration testing. 
 Desirable Microsoft Certified: Power Platform Solution Architect Expert (PL-600). Microsoft Certified: Azure Developer Associate (AZ-204) or DevOps Engineer Expert (AZ-400). Experience with Dual Write between F&O and Dataverse. Exposure to Copilot Studio and Microsoft AI Builder. Experience in a regulated, multi-country enterprise.

Key Skills: Azure Devops,Application,Dynamics,Azure Logic Apps,C#,Plugins,Microsoft Azure,Azure Functions

title: Oracle Senior Developer
description:
Job Summary We are looking for an Oracle Senior Developer who can design, build and tune high-performing Oracle database solutions. You will own database objects end to end, from design through deployment, and keep production systems fast, stable and well documented. You will work closely with data architects, application developers and support teams. The role suits someone who enjoys solving performance problems and writing clean, reusable PL/SQL. Responsibilities Design, code, test and deploy database objects, including complex stored procedures, packages, functions, views, materialised views, triggers and sequences. Translate business and application requirements into efficient, secure database logic. Build and maintain data load, transformation and batch scripts. Manage database changes through version control and structured release processes. Performance tuning: Optimise slow-running SQL queries, PL/SQL blocks and database scripts. Analyse execution plans using Explain Plan, TKPROF, AWR and similar diagnostic tools. Apply indexing strategies, optimiser hints, partitioning and query rewrites to improve throughput and response times. Proactively identify and remove performance risks before they reach production. Collaborate with data architects to design relational database schemas, tables and constraints. Apply normalisation, referential integrity and other relational database best practices. Contribute to logical and physical data models and review them for scalability and maintainability. Identify, investigate and resolve production bugs, execution exceptions and performance bottlenecks. Perform root-cause analysis and implement permanent fixes, not just workarounds. Support incident and problem management within agreed SLAs, including on-call support when required. Write clean, maintainable and reusable code that follows agreed coding standards. Conduct peer code reviews and provide constructive feedback to other developers. Maintain technical specifications, schema documentation and data dictionaries. Requirements Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 4-6 years of hands-on experience in Oracle database development. Experience supporting production databases and resolving incidents under time pressure. Familiarity with version control (Git) and SDLC or Agile delivery practices. Ability to write clear technical documentation. Preferred skills Oracle certification, such as Oracle Database SQL Certified Associate or Oracle PL/SQL Developer Certified Professional. Experience with Oracle 19c or later, including partitioning, AWR and ASH reports. Exposure to ETL tools or data warehousing concepts. Unix/Linux shell scripting for job automation and scheduling. Experience with CI/CD for database changes (for example, Liquibase or Flyway). Working knowledge of a second database platform, such as PostgreSQL or SQL Server. Exposure to cloud databases, such as Oracle Cloud, AWS RDS or Azure SQL. Behavioural competencies Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a methodical approach to troubleshooting. Clear written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical colleagues. Ownership and accountability for the quality and stability of delivered code. Ability to prioritise and stay calm when handling production issues. A collaborative mindset and willingness to share knowledge with the team.

description:
> Sr. DevOps Engineer Location: Hyderabad, INDIA Work Mode: Hybrid Skills: DevOps;Python;CI/CD;Azure Experience in Years: 6 Type: Full Time Life Sciences Cloud, Revenue Lifecycle Management and nCino each carry configuration, data dependencies and business journeys that must move-and be verified-with every release. A Salesforce release is rarely just a collection of metadata. In an industry cloud, the change also carries business configuration, connected data, sequencing rules and critical journeys that have to remain intact from one environment to the next. That distinction matters. A deployment can complete exactly as planned while the wider business release still contains unresolved risk: a configuration dependency moved out of sequence, target data is not ready, or a process that spans several objects no longer behaves as expected. An industry-aware DevOps operating model makes those concerns part of the release itself. It combines the delivery automation already in Copado with reusable assets configured around the product, the customer s environments and the business process being changed. The release is not complete when the metadata deploys. It is complete when the industry process still works. The release boundary has changed Traditional release planning often begins with a list of components and ends with a successful promotion. Industry-cloud delivery asks a broader set of questions: Which configuration and connected data must travel with the code In what order must dependent assets move What must be true in the target environment before promotion Which critical business journeys need regression coverage Which controls should change based on release type, risk or policy These are not separate operational checks to be added at the end. They are part of the delivery design. The practical answer is an accelerator that packages three connected layers: data and configuration movement, release quality gates and Copado Robotic Testing (CRT) regression coverage. The Industry DevOps operating model Different industry processes. One connected release model. Life Sciences Cloud Programs and regulated delivery Care Programs, HCP Engagement, consent, participant management and patient-service journeys. Revenue Lifecycle Management Product-to-order delivery Product, pricing, order and runtime configuration across the revenue lifecycle. nCino Controlled banking change Banking configuration, connected data movement and regression for critical workflows. 1 Data and configuration packs Preserve the relationships and sequence required by the industry process. 2 Release quality gates Evaluate dependencies, configuration integrity, target readiness and promotion policy. 3 CRT regression coverage Verify the critical business journeys affected by the change. Copado delivery foundation Data Deploy Quality Gates Robotic Testing The accelerator layers are configured to the customer s object model, environments, release path and governance rules. What industry-aware means in practice The model is consistent, but the implementation should not be generic. Each industry product brings its own release surface and its own definition of continuity. Life Sciences Cloud: protect connected programs and journeys A Life Sciences Cloud change can touch Care Programs, HCP Engagement, consent, participant management, patient services, and product and order data. The delivery challenge is not simply moving each item. It is preserving the relationships that allow a regulated process to work as intended. An accelerator for Life Sciences Cloud can package the relevant configuration and data, check for drift or conflict, confirm target deployability and run CRT coverage across Care Program enrollment, HCP engagement, consent and patient-service journeys. The release team sees the controls in the same flow as the promotion-not in a disconnected checklist. Revenue Lifecycle Management: keep the lifecycle synchronized Revenue Lifecycle Management connects product, pricing, order and runtime configuration. These elements form a dependency chain; treating them as unrelated deployment items creates avoidable uncertainty around sequencing and target readiness. An industry-aware model packages the connected configuration, applies dependency and promotion gates, and tests the product-to-order journey after the change. That gives release leaders a clearer answer to the real question: did the revenue process remain coherent across configuration and runtime behavior nCino: govern configuration and connected data together For nCino, banking configuration and connected data must move under controlled promotion. A technically successful component deployment is only one part of that change. The accelerator packages the relevant configuration and data, validates them before promotion, and applies CRT coverage to the banking workflows that matter after the release. The result is a repeatable control model that supports delivery speed without losing visibility into operational risk. Three layers make the accelerator operational 1. Data and configuration packs The first layer defines the assets that travel together. It captures the object relationships, configuration scope and required movement sequence for the industry process. Instead of rebuilding that knowledge for every release, the team has a reusable package that can be maintained as the implementation evolves. 2. Release quality gates The second layer turns release knowledge into executable control. Gates can assess dependencies, data movement, configuration integrity, target readiness and promotion policy at the relevant point in the path to production. This makes the control visible, repeatable and tied to the release record. 3. CRT regression coverage The third layer validates the outcome at the level the business recognizes: the journey. The regression scope follows the affected process-Care Program enrollment, product-to-order, or a critical banking workflow-so the evidence says more than the deployment passed. The operating principle Move the connected assets, enforce the right control and verify the affected journey. The three layers work as one release model, not as independent tools or after-the-fact checks. An accelerator should fit the customer-not force a template Reusable does not mean fixed. A useful industry accelerator is configured to the customer s object model, environments, release path and governance rules. It should make a clear distinction between what can be configured directly and what requires extension. That distinction is essential because two customers on the same industry product may have different operating models, risk thresholds and release calendars. The value of the accelerator is the combination of proven delivery assets and a disciplined configuration process-not a claim that every implementation is identical. Once configured, the model also needs an owner. Through Copado as a Service, CloudFulcrum can operate deployment execution, sandbox operations, asset and gate maintenance, CRT suite extension, release reporting and readiness for platform releases. The accelerator becomes part of the day-to-day release system rather than a one-time implementation artifact. Start with one representative release problem The fastest way to determine whether an industry accelerator is useful is to apply it to a real change. A focused working session should leave the team with a delivery blueprint it can evaluate, including: Industry object and configuration scope Quality gates mapped to policy and risk CRT scope for affected business journeys Deployment sequence and dependencies Direct configuration versus required extension An operating path after initial configuration This moves the conversation from broad capability to release engineering. The customer can see where the accelerator fits, which assets are reusable and what must be adapted to the implementation. Industry clouds deserve a release model built around the process they run. When data and configuration movement, quality gates and regression coverage are designed together, Copado becomes the foundation for a more complete and repeatable industry delivery system. The ideal candidate should have strong hands-on experience with AWS services, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), CI/CD pipelines, Linux administration, scripting, networking, monitoring, and production support.
 The candidate should demonstrate strong troubleshooting, critical-thinking, proactive planning, and problem-solving skills, with a focus on improving system reliability and operational efficiency.
 Key Responsibilities Manage, maintain, and troubleshoot AWS cloud infrastructure and production environments. Automate infrastructure provisioning and configuration management using Terraform, Ansible, and Packer. Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, Git, and pipeline scripting. Write Python and Bash/Shell scripts to automate routine operations, deployments, health checks, and incident response. Monitor infrastructure performance, availability, logs, and alerts using CloudWatch and relevant AWS monitoring services. Troubleshoot Linux systems, network connectivity, DNS, SSH/SFTP, HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/UDP, DHCP, and WebSocket-related issues. Manage cloud security, access controls, secrets, vulnerability remediation, and auditing using AWS security services. Handle production incidents, perform root cause analysis (RCA), implement corrective actions, and proactively improve system reliability. Maintain infrastructure documentation, operational runbooks, backups, disaster recovery procedures, and effective shift handovers. Collaborate with development and infrastructure teams to improve automation, scalability, security, and operational efficiency. Demonstrate strong ownership, critical thinking, proactive planning, and the ability to troubleshoot issues independently. 
 Required Technical Skills Cloud Platforms and AWS Services Hands-on experience with AWS EC2, RDS, ECS, ECR, VPC, S3, CloudFront, Step Functions, Secrets Manager, Systems Manager (SSM), CloudWatch, EventBridge, Lambda, Inspector, GuardDuty, CloudTrail, DynamoDB, API Gateway, Route 53, ElastiCache, SNS, Cognito, and IAM. Familiarity with Azure Active Directory (Microsoft Entra ID) and identity/access management. Infrastructure as Code and Automation Terraform, Ansible, and Packer. Infrastructure provisioning, configuration management, and automation best practices. CI/CD and Version Control Jenkins, Git, pipeline development, deployment automation, and troubleshooting pipeline failures. Scripting and Operating Systems Python and Bash/Shell scripting. Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills, including log analysis, process management, permissions, services, and system performance. Networking Practical understanding of SSH, SFTP, DNS, HTTP, HTTPS, DHCP, TCP, UDP, and WebSockets. Knowledge of VPC networking, subnets, routing, security groups, network ACLs, and connectivity troubleshooting. Monitoring, Security, and Reliability Cloud monitoring, alerting, log analysis, incident management, root cause analysis, access control, and vulnerability remediation.  Experience and Qualifications 3-6 years of experience in SRE, DevOps, Cloud Operations, Infrastructure Engineering, or Production Support. Hands-on experience managing AWS infrastructure and supporting production environments. Experience with Terraform, Ansible, Jenkins, Git, Linux, and scripting. Ability to troubleshoot infrastructure, networking, deployment, and application connectivity issues. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and manage critical incidents. 
 Behavioral Competencies and Shift Requirements Strong critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and troubleshooting abilities. Proactive planning, risk identification, and continuous improvement mindset. Good communication, collaboration, and incident coordination skills. Ability to work under pressure and take ownership of production issues. Willingness to work in rotational shifts, primarily night shifts, with occasional morning shifts. Ability to perform effective shift handovers and provide timely production support. 
 Preferred Qualifications AWS certifications such as AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate or AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate. Experience with containerized workloads, cloud security, disaster recovery, and infrastructure cost optimization. Familiarity with SRE practices, including SLIs, SLOs, incident management, and automation to reduce manual operational effort.

Youll collaborate with highly skilled engineers, architects, and AI practitioners while helping establish engineering standards, reusable frameworks, and best practices that drive success across multiple teams. This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week.
 Role Overview And Core Responsibilities Role Overview: We are seeking an experienced and highly skilled Lead Engineer to design, build, and operate production-grade systems that span software engineering, cloud-native infrastructure, and AI-powered applications. The ideal candidate combines deep Python engineering expertise with strong cloud architecture skills on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and proven experience building and deploying Generative AI at enterprise scale. This role will define reusable engineering patterns and platform capabilities that enable multiple product, data science, and engineering teams to safely build, deploy, evaluate, and operate intelligent systems. The Lead Engineer will remain deeply technical while providing architecture leadership, mentoring engineers, and influencing engineering standards across the organization. 
 Core Responsibilities: Production Python Engineering: Design and develop high-performance, production-grade Python services and applications following modern software engineering best practices. Establish coding standards, design patterns, and reusable frameworks that enable teams to ship reliable software at velocity. API Design & Microservices Architecture: Architect and build scalable microservices and RESTful/GraphQL APIs using Python frameworks such as FastAPI and Flask. Define service boundaries, communication patterns, and data contracts that support distributed system reliability and independent team ownership. System Design & Distributed Systems: Lead the design of distributed, event-driven, and asynchronous systems that handle high throughput and low-latency requirements. Apply principles of concurrency, fault tolerance, and horizontal scaling to deliver resilient production architectures. Testing Strategy & Engineering Quality: Define and drive comprehensive testing strategies including unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end testing using pytest and related tooling. Champion code review practices, static analysis, and automated quality gates to maintain high engineering standards. Reusable Libraries & SDKs: Identify repeated engineering patterns across teams and convert them into standardized Python libraries, SDKs, templates, and self-service platform capabilities that accelerate development and reduce duplication. Cloud-Native Architecture (GCP): Design and implement cloud-native architectures on Google Cloud Platform using services such as GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, and App Engine. Establish patterns for containerization, orchestration, autoscaling, and resilient infrastructure that support production AI and software workloads. Data Infrastructure & Pipelines: Architect scalable data infrastructure using BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Dataflow, and Cloud Composer. Design data pipelines that support both real-time streaming and batch processing for analytics, ML training, and AI application data needs. Infrastructure as Code & DevOps: Establish infrastructure-as-code practices using Terraform and CI/CD pipelines with Cloud Build or equivalent tooling. Drive automation of build, test, deployment, and rollback workflows to ensure repeatable, auditable, and fast delivery cycles. Observability & Site Reliability: Implement end-to-end observability using Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, Cloud Trace, and custom metrics. Define SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets for production services and establish incident response practices that minimize mean time to recovery. Cloud Security & Cost Optimization: Establish security best practices including IAM policies, VPC design, secrets management, and workload identity federation. Drive cloud cost optimization through resource right-sizing, committed use discounts, and efficient architecture patterns. LLM Integration & GenAI Applications: Design and build production applications powered by large language models, integrating commercial and open-source models through well-defined abstraction layers. Establish patterns for prompt engineering, context management, structured outputs, and token optimization. RAG & Knowledge Architecture: Design scalable Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines using embeddings, vector databases, semantic and hybrid retrieval, reranking, and metadata-enriched knowledge stores. Implement GraphRAG and semantic models where appropriate to improve retrieval quality. AI Evaluation & Quality: Define engineering standards for evaluating LLM applications and AI agents. Establish golden datasets, automated regression testing, retrieval evaluation, groundedness measurements, task-success metrics, and structured-output validation frameworks. Model Serving & Inference: Design model integration and inference architectures on Vertex AI and equivalent platforms supporting commercial, private, and open-source models. Establish patterns for model selection, routing, fallback, versioning, latency optimization, and cost management. Agentic AI & Orchestration: Define patterns for production agentic systems including tool calling, workflow orchestration, state and memory management, planning and execution, human-in-the-loop controls, retries, recovery, and long-running workflows. Technical Leadership: Lead architecture and design reviews, resolve complex technical problems, establish engineering standards, and make pragmatic trade-offs across quality, speed, scalability, security, operational complexity, and cost. Mentoring & Engineering Excellence: Mentor junior and mid-level engineers, review technical designs and code, raise engineering quality across the team, and help engineers adopt modern Python, cloud, and AI engineering practices. Cross-Team Collaboration: Partner with data scientists, platform teams, security, architecture, product management, and business stakeholders to translate enterprise requirements into scalable, production-ready solutions. Technical Communication: Communicate technical strategy, architecture decisions, risks, trade-offs, and capabilities to engineering leaders, architects, product teams, and senior stakeholders with clarity and precision.

Demonstrated experience building production cloud-native applications on GCP and working with Generative AI or ML systems is required. Experience may span traditional software/platform engineering and newer AI engineering; candidates are not expected to have spent an unrealistic number of years specifically working with Generative AI. 
 Technical Leadership: Demonstrated ability to independently design complex systems, lead technical execution across multiple engineers or teams, influence architecture, and convert emerging technologies into reliable enterprise capabilities.

Familiarity with Java, Go, TypeScript, or another production language is advantageous. Strong knowledge of data structures, algorithms, API design, distributed systems, concurrency, asynchronous programming, software architecture, automated testing, debugging, Git, and engineering best practices. Deep hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) including GKE, Cloud Run, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Dataflow, Vertex AI, Cloud Build, IAM, and Cloud Monitoring. Strong working knowledge of deep learning and Transformer architectures, including tokenization, embeddings, attention, inference, and modern foundation-model architectures. Experience with PyTorch, Hugging Face, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or comparable modern ML/AI frameworks. Deep hands-on experience designing and building production applications using LLMs, Generative AI, RAG pipelines, vector databases, and agentic AI patterns.
